messages.subject: blavaan 0.3-4 is released
messages.body_plain:

Ed

messages.subject: bug in blavInspect(fit, "lvmeans")?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ed

I was looking at extracting means and sd for the factor scores, using blavInspect(fit, "lvs"). When I compare my data manipulation of my calculated factor means (from blavInspect(fit, "lvs")) to the factor means provided by blavInspect(fit, "lvmeans"), the matrices dont match, there is a difference on how the factor means as arrange. So, I am not sure if I am making a mistake putting the means in 1 matrix, or is this a bug in blavInspect(fit, "lvmeans").

Here is my example

# The Holzinger and Swineford (1939) example
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

fit <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939,std.lv <http://std.lv>=T,save.lvs=T,
            bcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"))
summary(fit, standardized=T)

post_draws <- as.matrix(blavInspect(fit, "lvs"))
head(post_draws)
dim(post_draws)
is(post_draws)
colnames(post_draws)

dim(HolzingerSwineford1939)

mns <- colMeans(post_draws)
## Factor ID
factid <- rep(1:3,each=nrow(HolzingerSwineford1939))
cbind(colnames(post_draws), factid)

## hand manipulation for factor means
mns_mat <- cbind(mns[factid==1],
                 mns[factid==2],
                 mns[factid==3])
dim(mns_mat)
head(mns_mat)

## automatic factor means
fact_means <- blavInspect(fit, "lvmeans")
head(fact_means)

## compare hand manipulation, and automatic blavInspect
head(mns_mat)
head(fact_means)

Thanks

messages.body_plain:
Can you post your full code, for me the following example works, with both JAGS, and Stan

library(blavaan)

## Not run:
model <- '
  # latent variable definitions
     ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
     dem60 =~ y1 + a*y2 + b*y3 + c*y4
     dem65 =~ y5 + a*y6 + b*y7 + c*y8

  # regressions
    dem60 ~ ind60
    dem65 ~ ind60 + dem60

  # residual correlations
    y1 ~~ y5
    y2 ~~ y4 + y6
    y3 ~~ y7
    y4 ~~ y8
    y6 ~~ y8
'

fit_jgs <- bsem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy, std.lv <http://std.lv>=T, target="jags")
stp_jgs <- standardizedPosterior(fit_jgs)
head(stp_jgs)
dim(stp_jgs)

fit_stn <- bsem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy, std.lv <http://std.lv>=T, target="stan")
stp_stn <- standardizedPosterior(fit_stn)
head(stp_stn)
dim(stp_stn)

messages.subject: Re: standardized posterior solutions from all mcmc chains
messages.subject_clean: standardized posterior solutions from all mcmc chains
messages.body_plain:
Rui

You are right. So far the standardized posterior names does not include a group id.

With multiple groups the parameters would follow the same order as in partable(), all parameters from group 1, then group 2, and so on. You can use partable to add the group id, like this

Hope this helps

## Not run:
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

fit_stn <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group="school",
                std.lv <http://std.lv>=T, target="stan")
summary(fit_stn)

stp_stn <- standardizedPosterior(fit_stn)
head(stp_stn)
dim(stp_stn)

colnames(stp_stn)

### use parameter table to set names with the group id
prt <- partable(fit_stn)
prt_names <- paste(paste0(prt[,"lhs"],prt[,"op"],prt[,"rhs"]),prt[,"group"],sep="_")

cbind(prt_names, colnames(stp_stn)) ## they match the order of the standardized mcmc

colnames(stp_stn) <- prt_names ## set new names to standardized posteriors

messages.subject: Re: bug in blavInspect(fit, "lvmeans")?
messages.body_plain:
Thanks, this appears to be a bug when you request "lvmeans" and
target="jags". It will be fixed in the development version tomorrow.

To verify the results here, it is helpful to use lavPredict() on the
blavaan object. This is somewhat unusual, because it yields factor
score predictions based on the posterior means of other parameters.
But it helps show that the "lvmeans" side is incorrect and the means
manually calculated from "lvs" are correct.

Ed

messages.subject: Save.lvs + a statistical question
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I was trying to save the factor scores in a bsem using blavaan, to later use them in other analyses. Using the save.lvs=T option constantly resulted in an error:

Error: $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors

In addition: Warning message:

The following error occured while calculating summary statistics:

  Error : cannot allocate vector of size 180.5 Mb

In my many trials, I also tried the option jagextra=list(monitor="eta"), which succeeded in saving the scores once, but not in a later rehearsal. All other options are default (burnin, adaptation, sample).

My model consists of two latent factors with 6 indicators each, and equivalence imposed on the factor loadings (has been checked as viable in a previous step, using lavaan as well as semTools).

I am using a laptop - is it possible that the analysis is too heavy for a laptop (even if fairly "strong" laptop with 7th gen i7, and 8GB of RAM)?

The statistical question:

I read in the lavaan g.group a response from Terrence Jorgensen that, if the factor scores need to be used later on, it should be done only if ".. you account for the uncertainty of the estimated factor-score values.".

My plan was to run six (for six waves) 2-factor cfa's with a latent congruency model (Cheung ,2009) "attached" to each of these cfa's, save the latent congruence factor scores (which, basically are second-order factors) from each of the six models (six waves), and then run a latent growth model on the saved factor scores for the latent congruency factors. Following the approach suggested by Terrence Jorgensen (use the 10000 estimates per person -and per wave in my case- as a multiple imputation) is just daunting in my case. Would using just the means ("lvmeans") of the 10000 samples also count as "accounting for the uncertainty"?

Thank you for your time.

Regards,
Stefanos

messages.subject: Re: Save.lvs + a statistical question
messages.body_plain:
Saving the lvs can take up lots of memory. In some cases, it is
possible to tell R to use more of your system RAM, for example see

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/46635073/increase-ram-use-in-r

or you might delete all other objects from your workspace, except the
ones you need for model estimation.

I think that "accounting for uncertainty" in factor scores would
involve the full posterior distribution of each factor score, not just
the "lvmeans" option. But maybe it is also possible to specify a
larger model (larger than individual cfas), where you specify the
growth model alongside the six cfas in one step. (as opposed to the
two steps of get factor scores from six cfas, then fit a second model
involving factor scores.) Under this approach, you wouldn't
necessarily need to save the lvs because everything would be estimated
simultaneously.

Finally, the "operator is invalid for atomic vectors" error should go
away with blavaan 0.3-4, which recently went to CRAN.

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Save.lvs + a statistical question
messages.body_plain:
Stefanos

Another way to account for uncertainty is to use the mean of the posteriors, and the standard deviation as a measure of uncertainty for the factor scores. the brms package allows you to this. like this

library(brms)
library(rstan)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)

N <- 100
dat <- data.frame(
  y = rnorm(N), x1 = rnorm(N),
  x2 = rnorm(N), sdx1 = abs(rnorm(N, 1)), sdx2 = abs(rnorm(N, 1)),
  sdy=abs(rnorm(N, 1))
)
head(dat)

# fit a simple error-in-variables model
# | se(sdy) = measurement error in the outcome
# me(x1, sdx) = measurement error in variable x1 with standard deviation sdx
fit1 <- brm(y | se(sdy, sigma=TRUE) ~ me(x1, sdx1) + me(x2, sdx2), data = dat,
            save_mevars = TRUE, chains = 3, iter=8000)
summary(fit1)

messages.subject: Re: Save.lvs + a statistical question
messages.body_plain:
Stefanos

This would be an example on how to use the posterior draws and then add that with brms

library(blavaan)

library(rstan)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

library(brms)

# The Holzinger and Swineford (1939) example
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

fit <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939,std.lv <http://std.lv>=T,save.lvs=T,
            target="stan")
summary(fit, standardized=T)

post_draws <- as.matrix(blavInspect(fit, "lvs"))
head(post_draws)
dim(post_draws)

colnames(post_draws)

dim(HolzingerSwineford1939)

mns <- apply(post_draws,2, mean) ## get mean of posterior drwas
sds <- apply(post_draws,2, sd) ## get sd of posterior drwas
## Factor ID
factid <- rep(1:3,each=nrow(HolzingerSwineford1939))
cbind(colnames(post_draws), factid)

## hand manipulation for factor means
## get posterio means in matrix format,
## row for subjects, and columns for factors
mns_mat <- cbind(visual_mean=mns[factid==1],
                 textual_mean=mns[factid==2],
                 speed_mean=mns[factid==3])
head(mns_mat)
## hand manipulation for factor sds
## get posterio sds in matrix format,
## row for subjects, and columns for factors
sds_mat <- cbind(visual_sd=sds[factid==1],
                 textual_sd=sds[factid==2],
                 speed_sd=sds[factid==3])
head(sds_mat)

## put means and sds in the same data frame
fact_scores <- data.frame(mns_mat, sds_mat)
head(fact_scores)

## regression in brms accounting for posterior distribution uncertainty
fit_reg <- brm(bf(visual_mean|se(visual_sd, sigma=TRUE)~me(textual_mean, textual_sd)+me(speed_mean, speed_sd))+set_mecor(TRUE),
               data = fact_scores, save_mevars = TRUE, chains = 3, iter=8000)
summary(fit_reg)
